newsitem.title: USA: California welfare ruling seen costing $35 mln.
newsitem.headline: California welfare ruling seen costing $35 mln.

text.p: Tuesday's court ruling on welfare changes in California could cost the state up to $35 million, Governor Pete Wilson said.

A Superior Court granted a preliminary injunction to prevent the use of emergency regulations to implement the cut-off of pre-natal care benefits to illegal immigrants as required by the new federal welfare reform law, Wilson said.
Instead, the court is requiring the state to use non-emergency regulations, which would delay implementation of the cut-off by up to seven months, he said.

"The decision is totally erroneous, takes California out of compliance with federal law, will cost California taxpayers approximately $25 to $35 million, and will be appealed," Wilson said in a statement.
